correctness.rationale: Every order-five de Bruijn rotation class is an Eulerian 32-edge tour beginning at its unique zero edge. Every tour corresponds to a single-cycle local matching from 2^16 assignments; an independent DFS traversal yields exactly the same 2048 distinct cycles. Each is checked for 32 unique length-five patterns and weight 16. Independent cyclic direct sums and prefix-sum tests agree per cycle and give the full histogram, 528 symmetry orbits and exact rational moments. Discrete antipodal interpolation proves evenness and positivity without enumeration. Exhaustive finite proof only.

value.rationale: The number of antipodal balanced halves is a natural full-period cyclic Abelian-square statistic on sequences uniquely covering all five-bit binary patterns. Global balance forces only an even positive count, whereas the sharp maximum 22, eleven allowed values, multiplicities, orbit split, and moments require nontrivial complete finite enumeration. It measures a natural incidence between cyclic de Bruijn coverage and exact half-cycle balance; it is not an arbitrary slice or a recomputation of the previously recorded six-bit Abelian-square spectrum. No broad-order extension is claimed.
